sections.h2: Who sets and who collects property tax in Fulton County?
sections.html:
Two county offices split the work. The Board of Assessors values every parcel, and the Tax Commissioner mails and collects the bills.

The Tax Commissioner's page says the office collects property tax for Fulton County government, Fulton County and Atlanta schools, the State of Georgia, and the cities of Atlanta, Mountain Park, Sandy Springs, Johns Creek and Chattahoochee Hills. Owners in other Fulton cities should read their bill closely, because each taxing body sets its own rate and lists it as a separate line.

The Census Bureau counted 1,098,791 residents in its July 1, 2025 estimate, spread over 526.70 square miles of land. That density, about 2,025 people per square mile in 2020, explains why a sale in Sandy Springs can carry a very different tax picture than one in Chattahoochee Hills.

sections.h2: Where are the Fulton County tax offices and what are their hours?
sections.html:
The Tax Commissioner runs service centers at several addresses, and most keep Monday to Friday hours from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The main phone line printed on the county page is 404-613-6100.

  • Government Center downtown: 141 Pryor Street SW, Suite 1113, Atlanta 30303.
  • Customer Service Center at Maxwell Road: 11575 Maxwell Road, Alpharetta 30022.
  • North Fulton Service Center: 7741 Roswell Road NE, Sandy Springs 30350.
  • South Fulton Service Center: 5600 Stonewall Tell Road, College Park 30349.
  • Greenbriar Mall Service Center: 2841 Greenbriar Parkway, Suite 124, Atlanta 30331.

The Board of Assessors answers valuation and exemption questions at 404-612-6440 and at boa@fultoncountyga.gov. Its main office sits at 141 Pryor Street, Suite 1018. Tax bills can be searched and paid at fultoncountytaxes.org, and notices of assessment are online at fultonassessor.org.

sections.h2: What did the 2026 Fulton County tax cycle look like?
sections.html:
The 2026 cycle ran on a temporary footing. Assessment notices went online on June 19, 2026, and the appeal deadline for most owners was Friday, July 31, 2026, so that window has closed.

The county mailed 2026 bills on August 15. Because the state had not yet certified the 2026 digest, those bills were temporary and used each jurisdiction's 2025 millage rate, under an order the Superior Court of Fulton County authorized on August 4, 2026. City of Atlanta taxes were due September 30, 2026, and Fulton County taxes plus every other jurisdiction were due October 15, 2026. The county said a refund or revised bill would follow only if the final calculation differs.

If you are selling a house here, ask the Tax Commissioner whether your parcel shows a final bill or a temporary one, and ask the closing attorney how the contract handles any later adjustment.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Fulton County assessment?
sections.html:
You file within 45 days of the date printed on the Notice of Assessment, and you can only contest the assessed value, not the estimated tax. The county takes appeals online at fultonassessor.org, by mail, or in person at its offices.

At filing you must pick one of three paths: a hearing before the Board of Equalization, non-binding arbitration on valuation only, or a Hearing Officer. Arbitration and the Hearing Officer route can carry fees. The county warns that an appeal can take months, and that you may receive a temporary bill while it is pending. Pay that bill, since unpaid temporary bills draw penalties.

The Georgia Department of Revenue adds that an appeal may rest on taxability, value, uniformity or the denial of an exemption, and that the Department cannot override the local board on an individual appraisal.

sections.h2: Which homestead exemptions apply in Fulton County?
sections.html:
A homestead exemption lowers the taxable value of the home you own and live in. The state's standard exemption is $2,000 of assessed value, and many counties add larger ones.

In March 2026 the Board of Assessors announced new school-district exemptions with no income test:

  • Fulton County School District: 25% of assessed value for owners age 65 or older on January 1, and 50% for owners age 70 or older.
  • Eligibility needs a homestead exemption in that district for at least 5 of the last 6 years.
  • Atlanta Public Schools district: up to $50,000 off assessed value for owners age 65 or older on January 1, which may combine with other APS exemptions.

These apply to school taxes only, and owners who already hold a basic homestead exemption and qualify get the discount automatically. Anyone who sold before January 1 of a tax year has no homestead claim for that year, and a buyer who moves in applies for the following tax year.

sections.h2: What happens to property tax when you sell a Fulton County house?
sections.html:
Georgia assigns the whole year's tax to whoever owned the property on January 1. The Department of Revenue says the law does not refund part of the tax to a seller who leaves mid-year, so any sharing of the bill happens in the contract and at closing.

The formula the Department prints is: (assessed value minus $2,000) times the millage rate equals tax due, with assessed value set at 40% of fair market value. Each Fulton jurisdiction has its own rate, which is why the Tax Commissioner's bill lists county, school and city lines separately.

Before listing, pull the bill for your parcel and check that nothing is past due. Georgia county tax liens are filed with the clerk on the general execution docket, and a title company will want any unpaid bill cleared. Ask the Tax Commissioner for a payoff figure if the bill is unpaid, and ask the closing attorney how the January 1 rule is handled in your contract.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers say about Fulton County homes?
sections.html:
Census QuickFacts lists a 2020 to 2024 median value of owner-occupied housing of $458,800 and an owner-occupied rate of 54.3%. Median gross rent is $1,732, and the county counts 534,663 housing units as of July 1, 2025.

Median household income for the same period is $95,292. The population estimate sits 3.0% above the April 2020 base, and the county recorded 9,660 building permits in 2025. For a seller, the mix of owners and renters matters when a house comes with tenants or needs repairs before a conventional listing.

faqs.q: When are Fulton County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The due date is set each year. For 2026, City of Atlanta bills were due September 30 and Fulton County plus all other jurisdictions were due October 15. Look at the date printed on your own bill, or call the Tax Commissioner at 404-613-6100.

faqs.q: What is the penalty for paying Fulton County tax late?
faqs.a: Interest starts the day after the due date and runs until the bill is paid. The county adds a 5% penalty on the 120th day and another 5% every 120 days after that, capped at 20%. Partial payments are accepted, but interest keeps accruing on the unpaid principal.

faqs.q: Can I appeal my Fulton County assessment after selling?
faqs.a: Appeals belong to the owner on the notice, and they must be filed within 45 days of the notice date. The 2026 deadline for most owners was July 31, 2026. If you sell before the next notice arrives, ask your closing attorney who will handle any appeal for that tax year.

faqs.q: Who pays Fulton County property tax at closing?
faqs.a: The contract decides how the bill is shared. Georgia law puts the full year's tax on the owner as of January 1, and the Department of Revenue says there is no state refund for a seller who leaves mid-year. Your closing attorney or title company prepares the settlement statement.

faqs.q: Do I need to file anything before I can get a homestead exemption in Fulton County?
faqs.a: Yes, you apply with the county. April 1 is the standard deadline, and the county said a second filing window opens during the 45-day appeal period. Owners who did not hold the home on January 1 apply for the next tax year. Call the Board of Assessors at 404-612-6440 to confirm what applies to you.
